posture.general_guide: Everything here is a general guide and a starting point. Edit anything, delete anything, add your own.
posture.record_only: These templates set up structure. They never give medical or legal advice.

templates.name: Nursing home
templates.subtitle: Long term stay in a skilled nursing facility
checklist: Write down the direct phone number for the unit, not just the main line
Ask for the current medication list and keep a copy
Ask who calls you when something changes, and how they reach you at night
Write down the room number, floor, and wing
Meet the assigned social worker and save the direct number
Ask for the written grievance procedure
Save the long term care ombudsman contact for your area
Ask when care plan meetings happen and ask to be included
Ask the business office what is covered and what is billed separately
Ask what the facility does with personal laundry and labeled belongings
templates.burden: The long haul. Care plan meetings, grievances, billing surprises, and watching for any talk of discharge.

templates.name: Short term rehab
templates.subtitle: A rehab stay after a hospital admission
checklist: Ask how long the stay is expected to last and write down the answer
Get the therapy schedule and write it down
Ask who to call for an update on progress, and when they are available
Ask what the plan is for going home, and where
Save the case manager's direct number
Ask how covered days are counted and where you can see the count
Ask what written notice you get if coverage is ending
Ask what equipment will be needed at home and who arranges it
Ask what follow up appointments will be needed
Write down who to call if you disagree with the discharge date
templates.burden: A clock is running. Coverage days, a moving discharge date, and getting the house ready before they arrive.

templates.name: Inpatient rehab hospital
templates.subtitle: An intensive rehab program in a hospital setting
checklist: Ask how many hours of therapy happen each day
Ask when the team meets about the case and whether family can attend
Save the case manager's direct number
Write down the direct phone number for the unit
Ask who updates the family and how often
Ask for the expected discharge date and destination
Ask what equipment or home changes will be needed
Ask whether the insurance authorization has an end date
Ask what happens if more time is needed
Write down the follow up appointments already scheduled
templates.burden: Team conferences and authorization end dates. A lot happens fast and the family is often the only one tracking all of it.

templates.name: Hospital stay
templates.subtitle: A planned admission or an emergency one

roles.label: Doctor in charge on the floor

checklist: Write down the names of the doctor and nurse on each shift
Write down the direct phone number for the unit
Ask what the plan is for today, every day
Ask whether this is a full admission or observation, and write down the answer
Save the case manager's name and number
Keep any written notice about coverage or appeal rights
Check the medication list against what you know
Ask what to expect at discharge and how much notice you will get
Find out who the patient advocate is
Ask how to get copies of test results and records
documents: Any written notices given at admission
templates.burden: Staff change every shift and nobody repeats what the last person said. Discharge can be announced with almost no warning.

templates.name: At home, cared for by family
templates.subtitle: No agency involved, the family is the care team
checklist: Write down every doctor and the pharmacy in one place
Write down which hospital to go to and why
Build the medication list, including anything over the counter
Fill in the emergency card, including allergies and blood type
Note where the advance directive and other originals are kept
Photograph the insurance and identification cards
List the equipment at home and who to call when something breaks
Write down who to call for what, so someone else could take over
Start a cost sheet for anything you are paying out of pocket
Tell one other person where all of this lives
templates.burden: There is no staff. The family is the whole system, so the emergency card and a handoff someone else could follow matter most here.

templates.name: Home health agency
templates.subtitle: Nurses, aides, or therapists visiting the home
checklist: Write down the agency main number and the after hours number
Write down the assigned nurse's name and usual days
Ask how many visits per week are approved and for how long
Ask what each type of visit includes
Ask who to call when a visit is missed or late
Save the ordering doctor's number
Ask how supplies arrive and who to call when they run out
Ask what written notice you get if visits are ending
Ask when the plan gets reviewed and whether family can be there
Save the billing contact
documents: Plan of care or doctor's orders
templates.burden: Different people come on different days and visits get missed. Tracking who actually showed up is the whole job.

templates.name: Assisted living
templates.subtitle: An apartment with help, not a nursing home
checklist: Write down the main number and the after hours number
Find out who the wellness director is and save the number
Get the service plan and read what the monthly fee includes
Ask what costs extra and how those charges appear
Ask who calls the family and when
Ask what triggers a reassessment that raises the fee
Ask how dietary needs are handled
Ask what happens if care needs grow beyond what they can provide
Save the billing contact
Ask for the written complaint process
templates.burden: The fee changes when the assessed level of care changes. Watching add on charges and reassessments is where families get blindsided.

templates.name: Memory care
templates.subtitle: A secured unit for dementia care
checklist: Write down the unit direct number and the after hours number
Find out who the memory care director and family liaison are
Get the care plan and ask when it gets reviewed
Ask who calls the family and when
Ask how access to the secured unit works for visitors
Put food preferences and dislikes on file, not just restrictions
Ask what happens and who calls if a resident leaves the unit
Ask how belongings and clothing are labeled
Write down a short page about who they are, what calms them, what upsets them
Save the ombudsman contact for your area
documents: A personal history and preferences page
templates.burden: You become the memory. Tracking what you observed over months is often the only continuous record anyone has.

templates.name: Comfort focused care at the end of life
templates.subtitle: Hospice care, at home or in a facility
checklist: Write down the number that is answered day and night
Write down the assigned nurse's name and visit days
Ask exactly who to call after hours and what happens next
Ask how often the aide and chaplain come
Ask what supplies and equipment are provided
Ask how medications are delivered and refilled
Ask who to call at the time of death, and write it down now
Note where the signed medical orders are kept, so they can be found fast
Ask when the plan of care gets reviewed
Save the bereavement support contact
documents: One page of important phone numbers
templates.burden: Everything happens by phone at unpredictable hours. Having the right number and the signed orders findable in seconds is the whole point.
templates.localization_note: Do not translate this label with a direct cognate for hospice. Use descriptive comfort care wording plus a plain explanation in each language.

templates.name: Dialysis
templates.subtitle: Ongoing treatment at an outpatient clinic
checklist: Write down the clinic number and the scheduling number
Write down the treatment days and the shift time
Save the nurse manager and social worker names
Write down the transportation arrangement and the backup plan
Ask who to call when a session is going to be missed
Save the kidney doctor's number
Ask how lab results are shared with the family
Ask about the holiday and closure schedule
Save the billing and insurance contact
Ask for the written complaint process
templates.burden: Three times a week, every week, plus rides. The logistics never stop and a missed session matters.

templates.name: Cancer treatment
templates.subtitle: Ongoing treatment and infusion visits
checklist: Save the navigator's number and the clinic number
Get the treatment calendar and write down the cycle dates
Ask exactly who to call after hours and when to call
Write down the scan and lab schedule
Ask which medications need insurance approval and check the status
Save the specialty pharmacy contact
Ask to speak with the financial counselor before the first bill
Write down the transportation plan for treatment days
Ask how results are shared and how fast
Save the insurance contact and the authorization reference numbers
templates.burden: Cycles, scans, and approvals all run on separate clocks. Insurance approvals expire and nobody warns you.

templates.name: A child in ongoing treatment
templates.subtitle: Serious illness in a child, across hospital and clinic
checklist: Save the care coordinator's number first
Write down every specialist and what each one handles
Find out who the child life specialist is
Get the appointment and treatment calendar
Ask exactly who to call after hours
Write down the school contact and any learning plan in place
Check which treatments need insurance approval
Save the pharmacy contact
Ask what preparation is needed before procedures
Ask to speak with the financial counselor early
templates.burden: Treatment and childhood at the same time. School, development, and normal life have to keep going alongside the medical calendar.

templates.name: Stroke recovery
templates.subtitle: Recovery that moves across hospital, rehab, and home
checklist: Save the case manager's number
Write down each therapy lead and their days
Get the therapy schedule
Ask who updates the family and how often
Ask what the expected path is: which place comes next
Ask what equipment and home changes will be needed
Write down the follow up appointments
Ask whether insurance approval has an end date
Save the primary doctor's number for after the transition
Ask what to do if progress stalls and coverage is questioned
templates.burden: Recovery crosses several places over months. Three therapies run at once and each move restarts the introductions.

templates.name: Dementia care at home
templates.subtitle: Caring for someone with dementia in the family home

roles.label: Adult day program or respite contact

checklist: Write down every doctor and the pharmacy in one place
Write down which hospital to go to
Build the medication list, including anything over the counter
Fill in the emergency card, including a note that they have dementia
Note where the advance directive and legal papers are kept
Write down the safety setup at home: locks, alarms, hidden keys
Save respite and adult day program contacts before you need them
Write down who the backup decision maker is
Write a short page about what calms them and what upsets them
Tell one other person where all of this lives
templates.burden: Around the clock supervision with no staff and no shift change. Safety, legal decision making, and your own exhaustion all land on one person.
